requirements: derive permissions from normalized operation graph, not product name or user prose alone
map every operation to provider API actions, resource types, and prerequisite reads
include read-only discovery, preflight, mutation, wait/poll, rollback, verification, and evidence actions required by the approved lifecycle
restrict resource ARNs/IDs/names, regions, tags, project/subscription, namespace and conditions where provider supports them
separate control-plane and data-plane access
separate bootstrap, execution, service, runtime and verifier roles
use explicit role allowlists for pass-role/delegation operations
respect permission boundaries, SCPs, organization policy, tenant policy and explicit denies
render native provider policy formats deterministically
emit one or more minimal policy documents grouped by role and lifecycle stage
include schema/version metadata and bundle/registry digest
do not include credentials, secret values, access keys or tokens
JSON/schema validation
provider-native policy syntax and semantic validation where available
action/resource compatibility checks
resource-scope and condition checks
wildcard/privilege escalation detector
role trust and delegation graph validation
policy size/statement limits
plan coverage: every required operation authorized and no unplanned operation authorized
deny precedence and effective-authority analysis when available
produce human-readable policy diff and machine-readable operation-to-permission traceability
require approval for privilege expansion, destructive changes, wildcard actions/resources, trust-policy changes, and state migration
bind approval to exact plan and rendered policy digests
use only an already authorized principal
apply in reversible, idempotent steps
never use policy creation as proof of effective authority
if denied, stop and emit AUTHORITY_GAP with exact missing authority and operator handoff
read back role trust, inline/managed policy attachments, versions, boundaries, and provider-specific effective constraints
compare observed state against desired digest and approved plan
detect concurrent drift or policy replacement
execute only operations listed in the approved plan
short-lived credentials and bounded session duration where supported
checkpoint each irreversible boundary
stop on scope drift, principal change, target mismatch, expired approval, or stale plan digest
verify deployed resource state and health
remove temporary bootstrap grants when authorized and safe
retain necessary runtime role only
write immutable or tamper-evident evidence receipt and sanitized execution ledger

coverage_model.coverage_unit: provider + capability + lifecycle_operation + resource_type + role + scope

policy_pack_types.purpose: Read-only identity, target, existing-resource, policy and capability discovery.
Explicitly approved role/trust/policy bootstrap only; requires privileged operator or delegated bootstrap authority.
Native IaC plan/apply/status/events/state/rollback operations for the selected engine.
Only network and compute resource operations in the approved graph.
Only required image/package/artifact operations for the selected deployment.
Only required database, object/file storage, encryption and backup operations.
Only approved DNS records, certificate domains and edge/CDN configuration.
Read-only status, logs/metrics/events/health and evidence read-back.
Only approved reversible rollback or explicitly approved destructive cleanup.

important_limitation: A generic policy pack cannot be guaranteed to be sufficient for every future deployment without knowing provider, target, resource graph and lifecycle. Sufficiency must be proven per approved plan by complete operation mapping; otherwise return AUTHORITY_GAP. Broad standing privilege is not an acceptable substitute.
